NJIT discloses sub-$650 PHD-Hand parts cost and planned design release

A new interview details the total parts cost and planned release of a linkage-driven hand that remains a prototype without tactile sensors.

Humanoids Daily ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 4Videos 2

New disclosures about an existing research project

In a November 19 Humanoids Daily interview, an NJIT researcher put PHD-Hand’s parts cost below $650, including servos, controller, printing material and steel rods. The team plans to release files in about a month. The paper already exists; the fresh disclosures concern cost and release timing rather than first publication.

Rigid linkages replace tendons

The five-digit hand has 15 actuated degrees of freedom, using three servos per digit with rigid linkages and printed TPU flexures. Upper finger joints move in a coupled relationship. Demonstrations cover 33 grasp types and in-hand manipulation, but some grasps remain imperfect and do not establish human-equivalent ability across tasks.

Force and durability need further testing

The team reports about 200 hours on one prototype with two steel-rod failures. Fingertip force and grip payload have not yet been measured, and tactile sensors are absent. The project page still marks files as forthcoming. The parts estimate is not a finished-product price, and a complete downloadable build package is not yet available.
